subject: EU/APAC data jurisdiction alignment — KMS & routing constraints
messages:
From: Sophie Gonzalez <sophie.gonzalez@aureliabank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data jurisdiction Qs for EU/APAC private grid (questionnaire attached)

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We started filling out the attached attestation and have a couple of follow-ups specifically around private deployments across EU and APAC:

1) KMS residency: can customer-managed keys be confined to an EU KMS cluster while the control plane remains in EU and edge compute lives in APAC? If so, what is the model for cryptographic operations that cross regions?

2) Egress and lawful interception: we need a short explanation for our legal team on how egress is controlled in a private VPC deployment and what proof-of-residency evidence Redwood can provide (audit logs, egress-only endpoints, packet-level traces).

3) Failover behavior: in the event of an APAC region evacuation, can you outline the steps for maintaining residency guarantees (e.g., frozen-data mode, traffic blackhole vs queued processing)? We need both the operational play and the failback timeline.

4) Latency / contract constraints: we have a vendor SLA that requires sub-120ms p99 within APAC for inference. If routing to EU is required during peak, how do you handle contractual exceptions and what mitigation controls exist?

Attached: Aurelia-Attestation-Questionnaire.pdf — we've highlighted the residency-relevant sections.

Can we get a written response by EOD next Thursday (12/10)? Also copying Liam (network) for any packet-level specifics.

Best,
Sophie Gonzalez
Head of Cloud Security
Aurelia Bank

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Gonzalez <sophie.gonzalez@aureliabank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data jurisdiction Qs for EU/APAC private grid (questionnaire attached)

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then details below so you can share with legal/ops:

• KMS residency: yes — customer-managed keys can remain in an EU KMS (HSM-backed). We perform crypto operations in-region where possible; for APAC-side workloads we use a remote-encrypt pattern where plaintext never leaves the APAC tenant nodes — only ciphertext blobs move if the operation requires coordination. We can provide key use logs and HSM attestation statements.

• Egress & proof: for private VPCs we support egress isolation (no public egress gateways) and can generate per-request egress audit entries with source IP, destination, and TLS fingerprint. For legal evidence we generally provide aggregated audit bundles plus a directed packet-capture export for裁判/forensic review under NDA.

• Failover: we support two failover modes — "graceful drain + warm standby" (preferred) and "frozen-data emergency". In graceful drain, APAC nodes finish inflight requests and we route new traffic to pinned APAC-compatible model variants in EU if customers permit cross-border processing; warm standby keeps a reduced-capacity APAC appliance ready for quick restart. Frozen-data mode preserves residency by halting cross-border processing; queueing is retained and replayed only after authorization.

• Latency SLAs: if routing to EU pushes you over your SLA, we can surface an SLA exception with a documented mitigation plan (e.g., reserved burst capacity in APAC, quantized model variant with lower latency, or temporary CDN-like edge-caching).

I'll let Marissa expand on network-level specifics and attach a simple sketch of the candidate routing options (initial-network-sketch.png). We're happy to produce a concise evidence package for your legal team — will include KMS logs, control-plane hop traces, and an egress audit sample range.

Can we set a 30-minute sync early next week to walk the legal team through the artifacts?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Data jurisdiction Qs for EU/APAC private grid (questionnaire attached)

Hi Sophie — adding network and ops detail in response to Jonas's summary. I kept each point short so your legal/ops can paste into the questionnaire directly.

KMS / crypto ops
- Model: HSM-backed keys in EU for customer-managed keys. For APAC compute we deploy a KMS proxy that performs wrapping/unwrapping primitives locally when allowed; otherwise we perform remote-sign/encrypt operations over mTLS to the EU HSM. The proxy keeps no long-term plaintext.
- Evidence: HSM attestation sigs (chain), per-key use audit log (ISO-8601), and per-operation latency metrics. We'll include a sample CSV in the evidence bundle.

Egress controls & proofs
- Topology: Private VPC with egress blackhole by default. Outbound endpoints require explicit allowlist.
- Proofs: per-request egress entries (timestamp, source ENI, dest IP/port, ASN), plus a network flow export for requested time windows. We can provide signed flow exports (MD5+timestamp) and a short packet-snip under NDA.

Failover behavior (operational playbook)
- Normal: APAC primary -> EU replication for metadata only. Warm standby: reduced-capacity nodes in APAC hot-warm pool (RPO < 5s for KV state).
- Emergency frozen-data: we place APAC tenants into read-only/blocked outbound mode; control plane accepts a signed escalation from customer's SRE to allow cross-border processing.
- Timeline: warm standby -> full capacity typically 12–24 hours depending on instance provisioning window and model warmup. Frozen-data -> authorized cross-border processing is manual and documented (ticket + signed approval).

Latency SLA mitigations
- Short-term: deploy quantized 8-bit variant in APAC to reduce inference time and memory footprint (no cross-border).
- Mid-term: reserve dedicated burst capacity in APAC (we can commit a small reserved pool under a short addendum).
- Contract handling: when cross-border routing is unavoidable, we provide an SLA exception log and remediation plan; for critical SLAs we recommend a dedicated capacity contract.

Attachments: network-diagram-v2.pdf (annotated routing options), kms-constraints-summary.xlsx (key use examples).

If it helps, we can produce a 1-page "Proof of Residency" artifact that combines the HSM attestations, egress logs sample, and the failover decision tree. Let us know if you want that as a signed/dated bundle.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas/Marissa — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple of follow-ups and next steps: 

1) Please prepare the 1-page "Proof of Residency" bundle you mentioned. The legal team will need HSM attestation, one week's sample of signed egress logs, and a short statement on the authorization flow for frozen-data -> cross-border processing. We will send an NDA amendment for the packet-snip.

2) For the latency SLA: can you put together a short costs estimate for (a) reserved burst capacity in APAC and (b) an 8-bit quantized model variant validation run (we have a small perf test bed to help). We need those numbers to evaluate whether to sign the addendum.

3) Requesting a 30-minute walkthrough next Tue (12/14) 09:00 APAC / 01:00 EU — Liam, Sophie (us) prefer morning APAC; can you confirm availability?

If you can drop the evidence bundle and the two cost bullets by EOD Monday (12/13) it will keep our procurement timeline moving.

Best,
Sophie
Head of Cloud Security, Aurelia Bank
